messages:
Jamie: Quick question — proposal to make sampling TTL adaptive per-route based on sensitivity + recent error spikes. TL;DR: if a route's error rate crosses a threshold we temporarily raise sampling TTL from 1h -> 24h so follow-ups can be correlated. Thoughts?

Ajay: Concern: increasing TTL=longer retention of potentially PII-containing payloads. We need an explicit consent/consent-tier check and stronger hashing before extending TTL. Also, quota impact: longer TTL eats our inspect budget.

Lina: I like the correlation benefit for debugging, especially for async retries. Two quick thoughts: 1) make the spike window short (e.g., 5m) so we don't blow budgets on transient blips, 2) surface the projected quota cost in the UI so PMs/owners can approve.

Sofia: UX idea: in the Console route settings show a checkbox "auto-extend sampling on incidents" with a small preview: "will consume ~X inspect credits / hour while active" and a soft guard: requires two-step confirmation for high-sensitivity routes.

Ajay: Config sketch (prototype):
```yaml
sampling:
  default_ttl_secs: 3600  # 1h
  spike_policy:
    error_rate_threshold_pct: 3
    window_secs: 300  # 5m
    extended_ttl_secs: 86400  # 24h
    max_extended_per_day: 1000  # route quota guard
  consent_check: true  # only extend if consent tier >= "audit"
  pii_prehash: true  # fast hash before storing KV for extended TTL
```
This enforces per-route budget and consent.

Jamie: Nice. How should router enforce when quota is exhausted? Fallback to sampling=off or to minimal metadata-only capture? We should avoid silently dropping traces.

Ajay: Router decision flow (pseudo):
```python
if route.spike and route.quota >= cost_for_extension and consent_ok:
    enable_extended_sampling(route)
elif route.spike and route.quota < cost_for_extension:
    enable_metadata_only(route)  # no payload, just provenance
else:
    keep_default_sampling(route)
```
Metadata-only captures include headers, request size, anonymized provenance id — enough to triage without full payload.

Lina: Need to update dashboards: add a "spike-extended-sampling" metric and show cost burned vs budget per route. Also alert if we hit >50% of daily extended quota so SREs can decide to pause auto-extend.

Sofia: For rollout UX, propose canary: enable auto-extend only for routes tagged with `debuggable=true` and initially only 1% of traffic. Console should show a one-click ramp to 10/25/100% with projected cost delta.

Jamie: Thoughts on PII treatment when extended_ttl is active? Ajay suggested prehashing; we should also store an audit line with hash algorithm + salt id so audits can re-evaluate later.

Ajay: Yes — keep salt id and algorithm version in the metadata, but never store raw salt with the payload. And rotate salts monthly. Also add a scrub pipeline step before any human inspect flow.

engops-bot: deploybot: canary rollout queued: sampling/ttl-spike-policy v0.3 -> staging (1% traffic) at 2025-09-03T22:00Z :rocket:

Jamie: OK looks like we have consensus on approach + safety guards: consent check, per-route daily cap, metadata-only fallback, console cost preview, canary flow. Action items: Ajay -> update router PR with quota checks; Lina -> dashboard panel + alert; Sofia -> console checkbox + ramp UI; Jamie -> write short runbook for oncall.

Lina: quick Q — what metric to use for "error rate"? 5xx only or include 4xx? I'd vote 5xx only, otherwise noisy.

Ajay: Agreed, 5xx only for the spike. If product wants 4xx+ we can add separate policy.

Jamie: Cool. I'll open the RFC with the config sketch above and link PRs. Thanks all :thumbsup:
